title: Ärisaladuse kaitse seadus
description: Transposition of the EU Trade Secrets Directive (EU) 2016/943. Establishes the legal framework for the protection of trade secrets in Estonia, including definitions, remedies for misappropriation, and preservation of confidentiality in legal proceedings.

provisions.title: § 1. Purpose and scope
provisions.content: This Act establishes the rules for the protection of trade secrets against their unlawful acquisition, use, and disclosure, implementing Directive (EU) 2016/943 of the European Parliament and of the Council on the protection of undisclosed know-how and business information (trade secrets) against their unlawful acquisition, use, and disclosure.

provisions.title: § 2. Trade secret
provisions.content: A trade secret is information which meets all of the following requirements: (1) it is secret in the sense that it is not, as a body or in the precise configuration and assembly of its components, generally known among or readily accessible to persons within the circles that normally deal with the kind of information in question; (2) it has commercial value because it is secret; (3) it has been subject to reasonable steps under the circumstances, by the person lawfully in control of the information, to keep it secret.

provisions.title: § 3. Trade secret holder
provisions.content: A trade secret holder is any natural or legal person lawfully controlling a trade secret. The trade secret holder has the right to prevent the unlawful acquisition, use, or disclosure of the trade secret. Multiple persons may be holders of the same trade secret if they have independently developed or lawfully acquired the information.

provisions.title: § 4. Lawful acquisition of trade secrets
provisions.content: The acquisition of a trade secret shall be considered lawful when obtained by: (1) independent discovery or creation; (2) observation, study, disassembly, or testing of a product or object that has been made available to the public or that is lawfully in the possession of the acquirer; (3) the exercise of the right of workers or workers' representatives to information and consultation; (4) any other practice which, under the circumstances, is in conformity with honest commercial practices.

provisions.title: § 5. Unlawful acquisition of trade secrets
provisions.content: The acquisition of a trade secret without the consent of the trade secret holder is unlawful when carried out by: (1) unauthorised access to, appropriation of, or copying of any documents, objects, materials, substances, or electronic files lawfully under the control of the trade secret holder which contain the trade secret or from which the trade secret can be deduced; (2) any other conduct which, under the circumstances, is contrary to honest commercial practices. A trade secret acquired through breach of contract, breach of confidence, or inducement to breach is also unlawful.

provisions.title: § 6. Unlawful use and disclosure
provisions.content: The use or disclosure of a trade secret is unlawful when it is carried out without the consent of the trade secret holder by a person who: (1) has acquired the trade secret unlawfully; (2) is in breach of a confidentiality agreement or any other duty not to disclose the trade secret; (3) is in breach of a contractual or other duty to limit the use of the trade secret. The production, offering, or placing on the market of infringing goods, or the importation, export, or storage of such goods, is also unlawful.

provisions.title: § 7. Exceptions — freedom of expression and whistleblowing
provisions.content: The acquisition, use, or disclosure of a trade secret shall be considered lawful to the extent required for: (1) exercising the right to freedom of expression and information, including journalistic sources; (2) revealing misconduct, wrongdoing, or illegal activity, provided that the person acted for the purpose of protecting the general public interest (whistleblowing); (3) disclosure by workers to their representatives in the exercise of their functions; (4) the protection of a legitimate interest recognised by law.

provisions.title: § 8. Limitation period
provisions.content: The claim for remedies for the unlawful acquisition, use, or disclosure of a trade secret is subject to a limitation period of three years from the date on which the trade secret holder became aware or should have become aware of the unlawful conduct and the identity of the infringer. In any case, the claim shall be time-barred six years from the date of the unlawful act.

provisions.title: § 9. Provisional and precautionary measures
provisions.content: A court may, at the request of the trade secret holder, order provisional and precautionary measures against the alleged infringer, including: (1) cessation of or prohibition of the use or disclosure of the trade secret on a provisional basis; (2) prohibition of the production, offering, placing on the market, or use of infringing goods; (3) seizure or delivery up of suspected infringing goods; (4) prohibition of the importation or export of infringing goods. The court may require the applicant to provide a security or equivalent assurance.

provisions.title: § 10. Injunctions and corrective measures
provisions.content: Where a court finds that a trade secret has been unlawfully acquired, used, or disclosed, the court may order: (1) cessation of the unlawful conduct; (2) prohibition of the production, offering, placing on the market, or use of infringing goods; (3) destruction of all or part of any document, object, material, substance, or electronic file containing the trade secret; (4) recall of infringing goods from the market; (5) depriving the infringing goods of their infringing quality.

provisions.title: § 11. Damages
provisions.content: The trade secret holder is entitled to compensation for damage actually suffered as a result of the unlawful acquisition, use, or disclosure. When determining damages, the court shall take into account: (1) negative economic consequences, including lost profits; (2) unfair profits made by the infringer; (3) non-material damage, where appropriate. As an alternative, the court may set damages on the basis of the royalties or fees which would have been due had the infringer requested authorisation to use the trade secret.

provisions.title: § 12. Preservation of confidentiality during legal proceedings
provisions.content: A court shall take specific measures to preserve the confidentiality of trade secrets during legal proceedings, including: (1) restricting access to documents containing trade secrets to a limited number of persons; (2) restricting access to hearings at which trade secrets may be disclosed; (3) making available to non-restricted parties a non-confidential version of judicial decisions from which trade secret passages have been removed. Any person who gains access to trade secrets in the course of proceedings shall be prohibited from using or disclosing them.

provisions.title: § 13. Employees and trade secrets
provisions.content: An employee shall not disclose or use the trade secrets of the employer during or after the employment relationship, unless expressly permitted. A non-compete or non-disclosure agreement may extend the obligation for up to two years after termination of employment, provided that adequate compensation is paid. The general knowledge, experience, and skills acquired during employment do not constitute trade secrets.

provisions.title: § 14. Trade secrets in public procurement
provisions.content: Information designated as a trade secret by a tenderer in public procurement proceedings shall be protected by the contracting authority. The contracting authority shall not disclose trade secrets submitted by tenderers, except where required by law or a court order. The designation of information as a trade secret shall not prevent the contracting authority from fulfilling its obligations of transparency under public procurement law.

provisions.title: § 15. Relation to other laws
provisions.content: This Act supplements the Competition Act, the Law of Obligations Act, and the Penal Code in matters relating to the protection of trade secrets. Criminal liability for the unlawful acquisition, use, or disclosure of trade secrets shall be determined under the Penal Code. In matters not regulated by this Act, the general provisions of civil and commercial law shall apply.

provisions.title: § 16. Entry into force
provisions.content: This Act enters into force on 1 January 2019. This Act transposes Directive (EU) 2016/943 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 8 June 2016 on the protection of undisclosed know-how and business information (trade secrets) against their unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure.

definitions.definition: Information that is secret, has commercial value because of its secrecy, and has been subject to reasonable steps to keep it secret.
Any natural or legal person lawfully controlling a trade secret.
Goods whose design, characteristics, functioning, production process, or marketing significantly benefits from trade secrets unlawfully acquired, used, or disclosed.
